solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Irishman is admitting love, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: Pat is the stock crossword Irishman, short for Patrick
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An Irish fellow confesses to being in love, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat is the stock name for an Irishman in crosswords; 'admitting' puts love inside 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional dialect, a local way of talking.

clue.text: A top company outside centre of Hull — in port

indicators.note: outside says the first group of pieces sits around the next one

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letters of the word Hull

explanation.surface: A leading firm surrounds the middle of Hull, a port city in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the top company round the middle of Hull, which slots in before the company; Hull is a port in Yorkshire, England, though not the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a Pacific resort and port in Mexico, so an example of a harbour town.

clue.text: Go beyond nature and go wild

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the words before it run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Get past your natural instincts and run amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges NATURE and GO together; 'and' only joins the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrange is to have a greater reach than something, exceeding its distance.

clue.text: Work hard on article always as one promoting a cause

parts.note: to slog is to toil away
an is the indefinite article in grammar
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Toiling away on a piece of writing forever, like an activist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloganeer coins catchphrases for a campaign, a propagandist for some movement.

clue.text: Sort of post made of wood mum's put in

indicators.note: put in says the mother piece is placed inside the wood

parts.note: a forest is a wood
ma is mum, the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A post built of timber that mother has installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets mum inside the wood; 'made of' only links. A post here is a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A foremast is the mast nearest a ship's bow, a kind of upright spar.

clue.text: Salesman hopes to sell object thus, if you think that matters

definitions.text: Salesman hopes to sell object thus
definitions.meaning: a seller wants to get the full value of the item, its real price
a modest aside offering an opinion that may or may not count

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means at its true value and idiomatically hedges a remark as maybe unimportant.

clue.text: Wanting only the best in hotel, it is thought

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone thought to be in a hotel insists on the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist favours the select few, demanding top quality and excluding the rest.

clue.text: Sailor given order, losing heart, is to give up

parts.note: AB is able-bodied seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: losing heart says the central letter of the word for order goes

parts.note: to dictate is to give orders

explanation.surface: A seaman is told what to do, gets discouraged, and quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops the middle T of DICTATE, leaving DICATE; 'is to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to renounce a throne or duty, to relinquish it.

clue.text: Belief blokes should be housed in family apartment?

indicators.note: housed in says the blokes are put inside the belief word

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A conviction that chaps ought to live in a flat for the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a tenement block is only loosely a family flat; 'should be housed in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building divided into flats, often housing families cheaply.

clue.text: Designer of military show presented to the Queen

parts.note: a tattoo is a military display with music, like the Edinburgh one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A designer of a military pageant is introduced to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented to' only links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooer creates inked images on skin, so is a designer of sorts.

clue.text: Mess in the centre of study?

parts.note: mid is a prefix meaning in the middle of
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Asks whether a mess lies in the middle of a study room.
explanation.definitionFit: A midden is a dunghill or refuse heap, hence an untidy pile.

clue.text: Cross woman's wanting husband to look good

parts.note: to cut is to cross, as one road cuts another
Ada's: Ada is a woman's name, possessive kept

explanation.surface: An angry woman wants her husband to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' means the husband is wanted, so added rather than removed. 'Cross' looks like angry but means to cut across.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom for making a stylish, impressive appearance.

clue.text: I'm Scot messing about in TV programme

indicators.note: messing about says these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scotsman fools around on a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, short for situation comedy, is a kind of television series.

clue.text: Most magnificent match preceded by terrible rage

indicators.note: preceded by puts the scrambled rage in front of the match word
terrible says the letters of rage are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: The finest game opened with an outburst of fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges rage, and 'preceded by' says that scramble comes before the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest is the superlative of great, meaning grandest or finest.

clue.text: Fish of poor quality poet brought aboard ship

indicators.note: brought aboard says the pieces go inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship
tin as an adjective means cheap or shoddy, as in tinpot
Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: Second-rate fish that a poet brought on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought aboard' puts the cheap metal and the poet between the two letters of the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingrays are flat cartilaginous fish with venomous tail spines.

clue.text: Way unpretentious saint becomes invisible

indicators.note: becomes invisible says the saint letters vanish from the word

parts.note: modest means unassuming

explanation.surface: A humble saint fades from view.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or method of doing something.

clue.text: Average playing of violin — male leader, not female

indicators.note: leader, not tells us the first letter is swapped, the male one taking the female one's place

parts.note: fiddling is playing the fiddle, another word for violin

explanation.surface: Mediocre violin playing, with a man leading instead of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial F of FIDDLING becomes M. 'leader' refers to the first letter, not an orchestra leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling means moderate or ordinary, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Stop little woman keeping a father and son pinned down

indicators.note: keeping here means holding the rest beside and below her in this down entry

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, a woman
pa is father

explanation.surface: Halt the girl holding a dad and his boy immobile.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer DI 'keeps' the other pieces 'pinned down' beneath her; there is no container. 'Stop' is an organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is one of the main organ stops, a foundation register.

clue.text: Some racer, this! It's sure to win!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A punter marvels at a racehorse that cannot lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cert is short for certainty, racing slang for a sure winner.

clue.text: Glamour surrounds revolutionary model's movement popular with workers

indicators.note: surrounds says the glamour word goes around the turned piece

parts.note: charm is allure or glamour

indicators.note: revolutionary says the model word turns round

parts.note: to sit is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: Allure surrounds a radical model's popular labour campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the model word round and 'surrounds' wraps glamour about it. Chartism was a 19th-century British working-class campaign for the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was a working-class reform movement in 1830s-40s Britain seeking electoral rights.

clue.text: Verbally attacks plump boy

parts.note: round means chubby or plump
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone verbally lays into a chubby lad.
explanation.definitionFit: To round on someone is to turn on them with sudden criticism.

clue.text: Assertive about not drinking alcohol, one becomes badly behaved

indicators.note: about says the assertive word goes round the others

parts.note: brash means bold and pushy
TT means teetotal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pushy person on the wagon turns into a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts teetotal and one inside the assertive word; 'becomes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Brattish describes behaviour like a spoilt, unruly child.

clue.text: Specially designed bedroom — could it send you to sleep?

definitions.text: could it send you to sleep?

indicators.note: specially designed says the letters of the word are reworked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A purpose-built bedroom is so dull it might make you nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on a bedroom being for sleep; tedium may put you to sleep too.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium can make you drowsy, so a lack of interest might lull you off.

clue.text: Gin man briefly knocked back making exit

indicators.note: knocked back says the whole run is read in reverse order

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching animals
Ed is a short form of Edward, a man's name

explanation.surface: A man drinks his gin quickly and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns TRAPED round; 'Gin' is not the drink but a snare. 'making' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to leave or go out, a verb sense of making one's way out.

clue.text: Carry on with syndicate betting

parts.note: to wage war is to carry it on
a ring is a group of people working together, a cartel

explanation.surface: A gambling syndicate keeps placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagering is staking money on an outcome, gambling.

clue.text: Selected for team with other prisoners?

definitions.meaning: picked to play is to be in the side

explanation.definitionFit: Split as in side it means picked for the team; whole it is slang for imprisoned.

clue.text: Most well set to pass away with tears being shed all round

indicators.note: all round says the shuffled tears go around the dying word
being shed suggests the tears are cast loose and land in a new order

parts.note: the word tears is rearranged
to die is to pass away

explanation.surface: Someone is fully prepared to die with tears flowing all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being shed' scrambles tears into REAST; 'all round' wraps that round the word for pass away.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiest is the superlative of ready, most prepared.

clue.text: One works with lifeless arms

parts.note: suggests a person with limp limbs, but means a craftsman handling inanimate weapons

explanation.definitionFit: A gunsmith makes and repairs firearms, weapons that are not living limbs.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical offence by saint is unknown

parts.note: Simon is a saint, one of the apostles
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A church crime committed beside a saint is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the buying or selling of church offices or privileges, a church sin.
